proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/I)$ after choosing affine coordinates. Since $Y$ is a proper closed subscheme of $\mathbf A^m_k$, its defining ideal $I$ is nonzero; choose $0\ne f\in I$ and let $f_d$ be its highest-degree homogeneous part. Then $f_d$ is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial. If $d=0$, then $f$ is a nonzero scalar, so $I=(1)$ and $Y$ is empty; in that case any line gives the conclusion.

In the remaining case $d>0$, apply [lem-trf-infinite-field-top-form-direction] to $f_d$ and choose a nonzero $v\in k^m$ with $a:=f_d(v)\ne0$. Put $l=kv$ and choose a linear complement $W$ of $l$. In the coordinates $(t,w)\mapsto tv+w$, the coefficient of $t^d$ in $f(tv+w)$ is $a$, independent of $w$: only degree-$d$ monomials contribute to it. Multiplying this equation by the scalar $a^{-1}$ gives an element $F=t^d+\sum_{j<d}a_j(w)t^j$ of the transformed ideal of $Y$. No extraction of a $d$-th root or rescaling of $t$ is needed.

proof.text: Write $R=k[W]\simeq k[x_2,\ldots,x_m]$ and $B=R[t]/I$ in these coordinates. Since $F\in I$ is monic of degree $d$, polynomial division by $F$ shows that $1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1}$ generate $B$ as an $R$-module. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: Use homogeneous coordinates $[T:S]$ with $t=T/S$ on the affine chart $S\ne0$ of [def-sc-p1-standard]. The closed subscheme $V(T^d+\sum_{j<d}a_j(w)T^jS^{d-j})$ of $\mathbf P^1_k\times W$ contains $Y$, so it contains its scheme-theoretic closure. On $S=0$, its equation is $T^d=0$, which has empty zero scheme there because $T$ is invertible on that section. Thus the closure misses infinity scheme-theoretically. Finally $v\ne0$ makes $l$ one-dimensional, $W\simeq k^m/l$, and the projection to $W$ is precisely the quotient projection of the statement.

title: A linear projection finite on a proper affine closed subset, avoiding infinity
statement:
Let $k$ be an infinite field, let $m\geq1$, and let $Y\subsetneq\mathbf A^m_k$ be a
proper reduced closed subscheme [def-sbc-affine-space, def-weil-closed-immersion]. There
exist a one-dimensional linear subspace $l\subset k^m$ and a $k$-linear equivalence
$\varphi:k^m\simeq k\times k^{m-1}$ whose second component has kernel $l$. There is an
isomorphism, over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, from $\mathbf A^m_k$ to the fibre product
$\mathbf A^1_k\times_k\mathbf A^{m-1}_k$, whose two pullback components are the affine
maps induced by the first and second components of $\varphi$. The resulting quotient
projection $q:\mathbf A^m_k\to\mathbf A^{m-1}_k$ restricts to a finite morphism on $Y$
[def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Under the affine-chart map into
$\mathbf P^1_k\times_k\mathbf A^{m-1}_k$, the scheme-theoretic image closure of $Y$ is
disjoint from the infinity section $\{\infty\}\times_k\mathbf A^{m-1}_k$ [def-sc-p1-standard].
